experiment: tiled / zoomed inference for tiny-football proposals
reference: HUMAN_CONFIRMED_ADDITIONS only; existing GT is unverified

diagnosis.finding: Tiling raises recall from 23.0% to 27.4% at best. The 4.4-point gain is real but nowhere near the 80% target, and no threshold on any method reaches even 50%.
diagnosis.why_scale_is_not_the_cause: Human additions have a median width of 8.2 px against 6.9 px for existing source GT in the same images -- the balls the detector MISSES are slightly LARGER than the ones it finds. Cropping cannot fix a gap that size does not explain.
diagnosis.what_the_evidence_points_to: A viewpoint/context shift. 77.0% of human additions sit in the top band against 46.4% of source GT, and within that band the additions are LARGER (8.25px vs 6.25px) yet recalled far worse (29.8% vs 50.0%). Neither size nor position alone explains the gap; the cause is not established.
diagnosis.pipeline_sanity_check: On 30 images the same 3x3 pyramid covered 20 of 27 EXISTING blue GT annotations (74.1%), against 70.4% full-frame. Coordinate mapping, crop handling and dedup all work: the low number on human additions is a real measurement, not a bug.
diagnosis.CORRECTION_2026_08_14: An earlier version of this diagnosis, and the commit message b5f5846, said the missed balls are "an object the detector was trained to treat as background". That is NOT SUPPORTED and is retracted. Two facts contradict it: the source itself annotates non-active balls (22 human-confirmed), so there is no exclusion policy to inherit; and the detector recalls 50.0% of source GT in the same top band where it recalls 29.8% of human additions, so it is not blind to that region. No training set was inspected. The supported statement is a distribution/context shift of unestablished cause. See BALL_STRATIFIED_ANALYSIS.json.

workload_note: At 6.3 unmatched proposals per image the best union would put roughly 640 candidates in front of a reviewer for the 101 unresolved images, to recover about a quarter of the footballs present.
